name: Modern SEO M2 L1: Complete GBP Audit and Optimization
body:
> Module 2, 10:03. Source: Lesson 1 Complete GBP Audit and Optimization.mp4

## In short
- This is step 1 of the low competition ranking method from Module 1 Lesson 5: audit the Google Business Profile (GBP). The instructor says if the GBP is wrong, "not very much else matters."
- Start with a local rank map (heat map) so you know where the business ranks before you touch anything.
- The two most important checks are (1) primary and secondary categories and (2) every GBP field filled out.
- Build a long list of services from tools, remove duplicates, then use an AI prompt (Claude) to sort each service under the one category it fits best.
- Nothing gets changed on the GBP until the client approves. The audit goes to the client as a "GBP Review" document plus a questionnaire.

## Key ideas
- **Rank map first.** Before the audit, run a rank map, normally for the primary category plus the target city. In this demo he ran "driving school near me" instead, because the client already ranks first everywhere for "driving school Cedar Grove" and people in that dense New Jersey suburb area do not search by town name. (0:31 to 1:03)
- **Categories come first.** Check the primary category, then look at which secondary categories competitors use. Only keep categories that truly describe the business. He accepted "Driver's license training school" and "Learner driver training area" and rejected "Driving test center" (it is a school, not a test center), "Driver's license office" and car rental categories. (1:33 to 2:44)
- **Fill out every field.** Description, opening date, contact, chat, social profiles, hours, special hours, the "From the business" and other attribute sections. Blank sections are a gap. Most of the missing answers come from a client questionnaire. (3:15 to 5:25)
- **Check that links are correct, not just present.** The Facebook link was flagged as wrong because it used http instead of https. (3:46)
- **Service areas matter little.** He likes to see 20 service areas but did not stress about this client listing only New York and New Jersey statewide. The audit template itself says there is "little evidence that service area has an impact on ranking." (5:25)
- **More services, no repeats.** The client had a handful of services. He pulled many more from the GMB Everywhere tool, checked each for relevance, and made sure no service sits under more than one category. (5:25 to 6:31)
- **Activity checks.** Posts (only one post, five years old), photos (just a handful, add a logo), booking link (none, "not a big deal"), review responses (they reply to all reviews, good), Q&A (none). (6:31 to 7:32)
- **Make changes without disrupting rankings.** The intro promises this, and the method shown is: recommend, get client approval, then change. (0:01, 2:44, 3:46)

## Step-by-step process
1. Run a local rank map for the primary category and target city (or a "near me" search if people in that area do not search by town). (0:31)
2. Open a blank GBP Review document. Leave the top blocks (GBP URL, landing page, location, recommended landing page, H1 and title tag) for later; the landing page parts are covered in Lesson 2. (1:03)
3. In the GBP, go to Edit Profile, then business categories. Note the primary category. (1:33)
4. Open GMB Everywhere's Category Finder. Enter the primary category and review the related categories competitors use. Pick only the relevant ones. (1:33 to 2:12)
5. In the GBP Review document, mark "Multiple Categories?" as No and list the recommended secondary categories. (2:44)
6. Go back through every GBP section: description, opening date, contact, chat, social profiles, address, service area, hours, special hours, and all "More" attributes. Note every blank or wrong item in the review document. (3:15 to 5:25)
7. Copy the social profile links into the document so the client can confirm them. Flag any that look wrong (for example http instead of https). (3:46)
8. Note special hours for upcoming holidays as a to-do. (3:46)
9. List all unanswered attribute questions (ownership, accessibility, amenities, parking, payments, planning, service options) for the client to answer through the questionnaire. (4:21 to 5:25)
10. Check service areas. (5:25)
11. Open Edit services. Compare current services against the related services in GMB Everywhere, use "View more" and copy the relevant ones into the document. (5:25 to 6:31)
12. Review the pasted services: remove overlaps, make sure each is relevant to the GBP categories. (6:31)
13. Check posts, photos (and logo), booking link, review responses and Q&A. Mark Yes or No for each. (6:31 to 7:32)
14. Paste the categories and full service list into the Claude prompt and have it assign each service to its best-fit category with no repeats. (8:11 to 8:43)
15. Paste the categorized services into the review document. (8:43)
16. Send the GBP Review plus the questionnaire to the client to verify answers, services and categories. Make changes only after approval. (9:17 to 9:47)

## Checklist
- Rank map run before any changes (primary category plus city, or "near me" if needed)
- Primary category confirmed
- Relevant secondary categories identified from competitor research
- Description filled out
- Opening date filled out
- Chat set up
- Social profile links present and correct (https)
- Address correct
- Service areas filled out (up to 20)
- Regular hours correct
- Special hours set for upcoming holidays
- All "From the business" and other attributes answered Yes or No
- Services list expanded, relevant, and with no duplicates across categories
- Each service assigned to its best-fit category
- Posts going out regularly
- Enough photos, plus a logo
- Booking or appointment link checked
- Reviews responded to regularly
- Q&A section checked
- Client questionnaire sent
- Client approval received before any GBP change

## Tools and resources mentioned
| Tool or resource | What it is used for | Timestamp |
|---|---|---|
| LeadSnap heat map | Local rank map (grid of rank positions) before the audit | 0:31 |
| GBP Review document (Google Doc template) | Audit sheet with Item, Result, Suggestion columns; sent to client | 1:03 |
| Google Business Profile, Edit Profile and Edit services | Checking categories, fields and services | 1:33, 5:25 |
| GMB Everywhere, Category Finder 2.0 | Shows related categories, how many GBPs use each, and related services | 1:33, 5:59 |
| Client questionnaire | Collects answers for all GBP attribute questions | 3:15, 4:53 |
| Claude (Sonnet 4.5 shown on screen) | Prompt that sorts services into categories with no repeats | 8:11 |

## Numbers and benchmarks
- 673,000 GBPs use "Driving school" as their primary category, per GMB Everywhere (shown as 673k). (1:33)
- "Learner driver training area" shows 720 searches per month in GMB Everywhere's hover card (on screen, not read aloud). (2:25)
- Rank map shown on screen: keyword "driving school near me", average rank 11.15, top 3 coverage 15.98%, 13 x 13 grid (169 points), 1.00 mile between points. (0:45)
- He likes to see 20 service areas. (5:25)
- The only GBP post found was from five years ago. (6:31)
- The client had 385 reviews (on screen and in Lesson 2). (7:45)
- "If you get it right, you're going to be ahead of 90% of your competition." Instructor claim, not verified. (0:01)

## Terms
**Rank map (heat map):** A grid of points over the area showing where the business ranks for a keyword at each point.
**Primary category:** The main GBP category. In Module 1 the instructor says you rank first for searches tied to it.
**Secondary categories:** Additional GBP categories that describe other real parts of the business.
**GBP Review:** The instructor's audit document. Each row is an item, a result (Yes or No) and a suggestion for the client.
**Questionnaire:** A form the client fills in so the agency knows the correct answers for every GBP attribute.
**Special hours:** Holiday hours in the GBP. The template says to update them as new holidays come up.

## Worth quoting
- "If you get the GBP wrong, not very much else matters." (0:01)
- "The first and most important is the primary and secondary categories." (4:53)
- "Remember, we get client permission before making changes to the GBP." (2:44)

## How to use this at TAG
- **Run a baseline rank map for each client before any GBP change.** For Pipeliners, Alphalete and Summit AZ, record the current map so later changes can be compared (ties into Lesson 4's tracking advice). Kim's visibility tracker (memory file `project_visibility_tracker.md`) is a natural place to log it.
- **Do a category pass with GMB Everywhere on each GBP.** List the secondary categories competitors use and keep only those that truly match each client's services. Treat the list as a recommendation for Kim and the client to approve.
- **Build a categorized service list per client.** Pull related services for each category, remove repeats, and run the lesson's Claude prompt so every service sits under one category.
- **Check attributes and links field by field.** Note any http social links, missing special hours, unanswered attributes, missing chat.
- **Photos:** when recommending more GBP photos, follow TAG's standing rule from Scott's meetings (memory file `project_tag_meeting_decisions.md`): internal pipe damage or lining work only, never under-sink plumbing.
- **Approval first.** The lesson's rule (client approval before changes) matches TAG practice. Output the findings as a review document or fix list for Kim, not as direct edits.

## Open questions
- At 1:33 the transcript says "if I come in here to GMB, it's an old tool." Unclear in video what "old tool" refers to; the tool used is GMB Everywhere.
- Whisper wrote "GVP" several times (6:31, 7:02, 7:32). It means GBP.
- At 7:32 "If it did, we'd use the booking link or the home page" is unclear: possibly meaning the booking button would point to a booking page or the home page.
- The Photos and Q&A rows of the review document were mentioned but not shown on screen, so their exact template wording is unknown.
- The Claude output also suggested extra categories (Traffic school, Motorcycle driving school, Defensive driving school) and "keep 5-10 core services per category visible." That came from Claude, not the instructor, and he said "for now, we're just leaving a lot of this out." Do not treat it as course advice.
- "Ahead of 90% of your competition" is an unverified claim.
- No low-confidence lines in the manifest.

## Timestamps
- 0:01 Intro: step 1 of the low competition ranking method
- 0:31 Rank map first, and why he used a "near me" search
- 1:03 The GBP Review document
- 1:33 Primary category and GMB Everywhere
- 2:12 Choosing secondary categories
- 2:44 Recording recommendations, client permission rule
- 3:15 Description, contact, chat, social profiles
- 3:46 Wrong Facebook link, address, hours, special hours
- 4:21 "From the business" attributes and the questionnaire
- 4:53 The two main checks
- 5:25 Service areas and services
- 5:59 GMB Everywhere service finder
- 6:31 Removing duplicate services, checking posts
- 7:02 Photos, logo, booking link
- 7:32 Review responses and Q&A
- 8:11 Claude prompt to organize services
- 8:43 Categorized output
- 9:17 Sending the review and questionnaire to the client
